module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 120

*Reference:*
- [erdosproblems.com/120](https://www.erdosproblems.com/120)
- [St20](http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm1/fm1111.pdf) Steinhaus, Hugo, Sur les distances des points dans les ensembles de measure positive. Fund. Math. (1920), 93-104.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set MeasureTheory

namespace Erdos120

/--
There exists a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, dependent on set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$,
of positive measure which does not contain any set of the shape $a * A + b$
for some $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \neq 0$?
-/
def Erdos120For (A : Set ℝ) : Prop := ∃ E : Set ℝ,
  MeasurableSet E ∧ 0 < volume E ∧ ∀ a b : ℝ, a ≠ 0 → ¬ .image (fun x => a * x + b) A ⊆ E

/--
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be an infinite set. Must there be a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
of positive measure which does not contain any set of the shape $a * A + b$
for some $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \neq 0$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 28]
theorem erdos_120 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Set ℝ, A.Infinite → Erdos120For A := by
  sorry

/--
Steinhaus [St20] has proved Erdős 120 to be false whenever $A$ is a finite set.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 28]
theorem erdos_120.variants.finite_set {A : Set ℝ} (h : A.Finite) : ¬ Erdos120For A := by
  sorry

end Erdos120

reformulations.difference: The source asks for "a set E ⊂ ℝ of positive measure", meaning a Lebesgue-measurable set of positive Lebesgue measure. The Lean requires `MeasurableSet E` for Mathlib's σ-algebra on ℝ. That σ-algebra is `borel ℝ` (checked by `rfl`), so E must be Borel. The Lean also allows `volume E = ∞`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every Borel set is Lebesgue-measurable, so a Lean witness is a source witness. Conversely, suppose a null-measurable (Lebesgue) E with positive measure contains no aA+b with a ≠ 0. Then `NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq` gives a Borel t ⊆ E with t =ᵐ E, so t has the same positive measure. Alternatively, inner regularity (`MeasurableSet.exists_lt_isCompact`) gives a compact K ⊆ E with 0 < volume K, and K has finite measure. Any subset of E also contains no affine copy of A, so t or K is a witness in the Lean sense. Hence the Borel, Lebesgue, and compact (finite positive measure) versions all agree. Measurability itself is essential and is present: with only positive outer measure the problem would become trivial.

review.notes:
No misformalizations and no status issues.

Lean checks, run in /workspace/review:
(1) Sanity lemmas. `Erdos120For (range (Nat.cast : ℕ → ℝ))` holds with E = Icc 0 1, matching the source's remark that the answer is yes when A is unbounded. `¬ Erdos120For ∅` and `¬ Erdos120For {c}` also hold.
(2) Equivalences. `Erdos120For A` is equivalent to the version with null-measurable (Lebesgue) witnesses, and to the version with compact witnesses. Both proofs have no `sorry`.
(3) Finite variant. A full proof of `¬ Erdos120For A` for finite A, via `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet`. It uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. So `erdos_120.variants.finite_set` is true, as its `research solved` tag says, and could be closed if the maintainers want.

`erdos_120` itself is the Erdős similarity conjecture exactly. The answer slot has the source's polarity: `answer(True)` means every infinite A has such an E. The main open special case, A = {2^{-n}}, is not trivially decided by the definitions.

The erdosproblems.com forum records that an earlier formalization omitted measurability, which made Green's Problem 94 trivially refutable with a Hamel-basis set of positive outer measure. The current `Erdos120For` includes `MeasurableSet E`, so this file is not affected.

Two cosmetic slips in the module docstring's reference, not reported as findings because the mathematics is unaffected:
- The Steinhaus title reads "ensembles de measure positive". It should be "mesure positive" (JLM24 bibliography: "Sur les distances des points dans les ensembles de mesure positive", Fund. Math. 1 (1920), 93–104).
- The volume number 1 is omitted.

The attribution of the finite case to Steinhaus is copied from erdosproblems.com. JLM24 calls it "often attributed to H. Steinhaus". It has no bearing on the statement.

Status: open on erdosproblems.com (read 2026-09-23; page last edited 23 Jan 2026) and in the teorth database. The only claimed full proof, arXiv:2001.02395, was withdrawn. The 2026 papers prove special cases only.
